title: Childbirth classes
what: These are classes for pregnant women and their partners. You learn how birth goes, how to breathe, and how to care for your baby.
why: Usually in the second half of pregnancy. Especially useful before a first birth.
duration: usually several classes of 1 to 2 hours
tell_doctor: How many weeks pregnant you are
If your doctor has limited your physical activity
If you feel unwell on the day of a class

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear comfortable clothes you can lie on a mat and exercise in.

prepare.title: Questions
prepare.text: Write down what worries you: contractions, pain relief, breastfeeding.

prepare.title: Partner
prepare.text: Find out if your partner can come to all or some of the classes.

steps: The instructor gets to know the group
You learn how labor starts and when to go to the maternity hospital
You are shown how to breathe and which positions ease contractions
You learn how your partner can help
You learn about breastfeeding and baby care
feel: If you get tired or feel unwell, tell the instructor. You can rest
after: Practice breathing and positions at home
Pack your hospital bag ahead of time
Talk with your doctor about your wishes for the birth
red_flags: Contractions, bleeding, or leaking fluid: call your doctor or emergency services
Your baby is moving much less than usual

faq.a: Usually from 20 to 30 weeks. Ask the clinic or school.

faq.q: Do I need classes if this is not my first birth?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but many people go to refresh what they know.

reminders.text: Childbirth class soon. Bring comfortable clothes and water.
